scope: Primary-source reviewed graphics/API translation layers missing from the catalog; APIs, implementation method, status, platform/hardware requirements, language/source availability, and release dates are recorded where maintainers document them.

projects.title: GL4ES
projects.game: OpenGL applications and games targeting embedded/mobile graphics (multi-title)
projects.platform: OpenGL 2.1/1.5 → OpenGL ES 2.0/1.1; Linux, Android, Emscripten, AmigaOS 4 and listed ARM single-board systems
projects.status: Active; the maintainer describes it as a desktop OpenGL-to-OpenGL ES translation library; repository updated 2026-10-14.
projects.summary: Translates legacy desktop OpenGL calls to OpenGL ES for systems whose drivers expose OpenGL ES rather than desktop OpenGL. It is used by applications and ports, not a game emulator.
projects.strategy: Desktop OpenGL API translation to OpenGL ES

sources.label: Maintainer repository and README: API direction, platform support, and project status

projects.title: Mesa Gallium D3D12 Driver
projects.game: OpenGL applications in WSL and systems with Direct3D 12 support (multi-title)
projects.platform: OpenGL 3.3 → Microsoft Direct3D 12; primarily Linux applications in WSL/WSLg using a Windows D3D12 GPU driver
projects.status: Mesa documents this as an active Gallium driver that emits Direct3D 12 calls to provide desktop OpenGL 3.3, including as the WSLg graphics acceleration path.
projects.summary: A Mesa Gallium driver that emits Direct3D 12 calls rather than targeting a specific GPU architecture. Microsoft and Mesa document it as the OpenGL acceleration path for Linux GUI applications under WSLg when the Windows GPU driver supports WSL virtualization.
projects.strategy: Mesa Gallium OpenGL frontend mapped to Direct3D 12
projects.source_available: Public Mesa source repository (component licenses vary)

sources.label: Mesa D3D12 driver documentation: API target and OpenGL support
Microsoft WSLg documentation: D3D12-backed Mesa OpenGL acceleration

projects.title: KosmicKrisp
projects.game: Vulkan applications on Apple Silicon Macs (multi-title)
projects.platform: Vulkan 1.4 → Metal 4; macOS 26 or newer on Apple Silicon
projects.status: Khronos-conformant Vulkan 1.4 Mesa driver as of 2026-10-01; requires Apple Silicon, Metal 4, and macOS 26 or newer.
projects.summary: A Mesa Vulkan driver layered on Apple Metal for Apple Silicon Macs. Khronos reports that it passed Vulkan 1.4 conformance testing on 2026-10-01; the Vulkan SDK distributes a conformant build.
projects.strategy: Vulkan driver implementation on top of Metal 4
projects.source_available: Public Mesa source repository (MIT/X11 and other component licenses)

sources.label: Mesa KosmicKrisp documentation: API, OS, and hardware requirements
Khronos conformance announcement: Vulkan 1.4 status and date

projects.title: DXGL
projects.platform: DirectDraw/Direct3D 7-era calls → OpenGL; Windows 10 or newer standard build, Windows XP SP3 or newer legacy build; also usable under Wine
projects.status: Active; 0.5.28 was released 2026-10-14. The README says the 0.6.0-dev branch is nonfunctional and directs users to 0.5.x; DirectDraw 1–7 support is partial and 3D remains incomplete.
projects.summary: A DirectDraw replacement wrapper that maps legacy 2D and some 3D API behavior to OpenGL. The maintainer lists OpenGL 2.0 with framebuffer-object and non-power-of-two texture support as the minimum, recommends OpenGL 3.2+, and requires SSE2 for the standard build.
projects.strategy: Legacy DirectDraw/Direct3D calls wrapped over OpenGL

sources.label: Maintainer README: API coverage, branch caveat, and hardware/OS requirements

projects.title: cnc-ddraw
projects.platform: DirectDraw software-renderer API → GDI, OpenGL, or Direct3D 9; Windows ME through Windows 11 and Wine on Linux/macOS/Android
projects.status: Active source repository; the maintainer lists Windows ME/2000/XP through Windows 11 and Wine hosts. Formal release page and current source activity differ, so no latest numbered release is claimed here.
projects.summary: A DirectDraw API reimplementation with selectable GDI, OpenGL, and Direct3D 9 output backends for classic 2D software-rendered games. The project explicitly says it does not support games that render through Direct3D.
projects.strategy: DirectDraw API reimplementation with GDI/OpenGL/Direct3D 9 renderers

sources.label: Maintainer README: renderer choices, supported systems, and Direct3D-game limitation

projects.title: dgVoodoo2
projects.platform: Glide 2/3, DirectX 1–7, Direct3D 8.1/9 → Direct3D 11/12 or Microsoft WARP; Windows 7 or newer
projects.status: Active proprietary wrapper; maintainer README identifies version 2.87.5, re-released 2026-09-15. Output options include D3D feature levels 10.0, 10.1, 11.0, 12.0 and WARP software rendering, with documented limitations on older feature levels.
projects.summary: Implements legacy Glide and DirectX graphics interfaces over modern Direct3D 11/12 for old Windows software. This is a graphics-API compatibility wrapper, not a whole-system emulator; the implementation source is not published.
projects.strategy: Legacy graphics API implementations over Direct3D 11/12 or WARP
projects.source_available: Proprietary; maintainer provides binary packages and documentation, no source repository

sources.label: Maintainer dgVoodoo2 readme: APIs, output backends, Windows support, and current version

projects.title: nGlide
projects.platform: Glide 2.11/2.60/3.10 → Direct3D or Vulkan; Windows XP/7/8/10/11, with a DirectX 9.0- or Vulkan 1.0-capable GPU
projects.status: The developer currently lists freeware version 2.10 and supports Glide 2.11/2.60/3.10 through Direct3D or Vulkan. The developer announced the first public release, version 0.90, on 2009-11-07.
projects.summary: A Windows Glide wrapper for running applications written for 3dfx Glide without a Voodoo graphics card. It accepts three Glide DLL/API versions and renders through Direct3D or Vulkan; DOS Glide use requires a separately patched DOSBox build.
projects.strategy: Glide API wrapper over Direct3D or Vulkan
projects.source_available: Proprietary freeware; binary downloads and documentation only

sources.label: Developer nGlide page: Glide versions, backends, OS/GPU requirements, and version
Developer announcement of first public release (2009-11-07)

projects.title: Gallium Nine Standalone
projects.game: Direct3D 9 applications and games under Wine (multi-title)
projects.platform: Direct3D 9 → Mesa Gallium driver; Linux through Wine; requires a Gallium-based Mesa driver and Mesa Nine state tracker
projects.status: Latest listed release is v0.10 (2024-10-06); current maintenance status is unclear. It implements the Wine side of Gallium Nine and relies on Mesa’s D3D9 frontend and a compatible Gallium driver.
projects.summary: A standalone Wine component that exposes the Mesa Gallium Nine Direct3D 9 implementation to stock Wine without patched Wine builds. It bypasses WineD3D’s traditional D3D9-to-OpenGL path; DRI3 is the preferred lower-overhead backend and DRI2 is documented as a fallback.
projects.strategy: Wine D3D9 interface connected directly to Mesa Gallium Nine
projects.subtype: Wine D3D9 integration for Mesa Gallium Nine

sources.label: Maintainer README: integration model, requirements, and backends
Mesa documentation for the Nine Direct3D 9 frontend

projects.title: Valve ToGL
projects.game: Direct3D 9 rendering in Valve Source 1 software (multi-title)
projects.platform: Limited Direct3D 9.0c subset → OpenGL; used by Valve Source 1 rendering paths on Linux/macOS, but the public repository is an unsupported source dump
projects.status: Public source dump; Valve says it supports only a limited D3D9 subset, has some Shader Model 3 support, is supplied as-is, and most likely will not build by itself.
projects.summary: Valve’s ToGL is a Direct3D-to-OpenGL abstraction layer with a bytecode-level HLSL-to-GLSL translator. The public code came from the Dota 2 source tree and contains Source Engine-specific behavior, so it should not be treated as a general, ready-to-build D3D9 translator.
projects.strategy: Limited D3D9 interface and shader bytecode translation to OpenGL
projects.source_available: Public source dump (Valve license file; unsupported and may not build)
